nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: سبّح اسم ربك and سبّح باسم ربّك are both correct. Abū Jaʿfar said: If he reckoned this on the basis of omitting the bāʾ, then [it fails, since] مررت زيدا is not permissible; and if he reckoned it as one of those verbs that pass on [to their object] with and without a particle, so that the meaning is one, it is not so, because the meaning of سبّح باسم ربّك is "let your glorification be by the name of your Lord". The scholars have spoken about the meaning of سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى with answers all of which differ from the meaning of [the phrase] that has the bāʾ. Some of them said: its meaning is "declare the name of your Lord, the Most High, transcendent, and exalt it above your attributing to Him what the polytheists attributed to Him", because He is الأعلى, i.e. the One who subdues everything, i.e. who is high above it. Some of them said: i.e. do not say al-ʿUzzā, because it is derived from العزيز, nor al-Lāt, because they derived it from their saying الله. Some of them said: the meaning of سبّح اسم ربّك is "mention the name of your Lord while you are magnifying Him, humble and submissive". And some of them said its meaning is "glorify the name of your Lord in your prayer, humbly, occupied with it". Abū Jaʿfar said: The first answer is the clearest of them, as was read [in transmission] to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ: Isrāʾīl narrated to us from Abū Isḥāq, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ recited سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى (1), he would say: سبحان ربي الأعلى ("Glory be to my Lord, the Most High").
الْأَعْلَى is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ربك, or of اسم; it is preferable that it be a naʿt of what [the vowel] indicates. [Translator's note: the closing phrase «لما عليه» is obscure in the source; since الأعلى shows no case vowel, the sense may be that it should qualify the noun whose position it agrees with.]

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: [سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى refers to] Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. He said:

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: He said: [وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى refers to] ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Umayya ibn Khalaf.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: He said: [النَّارَ الْكُبْرى is] Hell. Al-Farrāʾ said: the lowest of the layers of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
There are several views on its meaning. It was said: the souls of the people of the Fire are in their throats; they do not come out so that they might die, nor return to their places in their bodies so that they might live. It was also said: they do not die so as to find rest, nor live a life from which they benefit. It was also said: it is from the saying of the Arabs, when someone is in severe hardship, "he is neither alive nor dead", as the poet said: [al-khafīf] 559-
ليس من مات فاستراح بميت ... إنّما الميت ميّت الأحياء
(The one who died and found rest is not [truly] dead; the dead one is only the dead among the living.)

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
There are two views on its meaning. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى:] whoever purified himself of polytheism, i.e. became pure. Al-Ḥasan said: مَن تزكى is one whose deeds were pure. The other view is from Qatāda, who said:
مَن تزكّى [is one who] paid the zakāt of his wealth.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ means he affirmed that He is] One. He said: فَصَلَّى — he is saying: then he performed the five prayers. Someone else said: صلّى here means "he supplicated". The correct view according to Muḥammad ibn Jarīr is that the meaning is "he prayed, and mentioned the name of his Lord in his prayer with praise and glorification". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake according to the view of the Arabic scholars, because he put what is before the fāʾ after it, and this is the reverse of what the grammarians have said. The correct view is that of Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: [بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ:] if you wish, you assimilate the lām into the tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy: «بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا»; this is a reading by way of explanation. Abū ʿAmr read «بل يؤثرون» with yāʾ, on the basis that it refers back to الأشقى.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى (18): there are three views on its meaning. One of them is that His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, "and the Hereafter is better and more lasting" is in the former scriptures; this seems to be the school of Qatāda. It was also said: [the statement that] success belongs to whoever purifies himself, mentions the name of his Lord and prays is in the former scriptures. The third view is that by it is meant the surah, as was read [in transmission] to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ, from Sharīk, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: سبّح اسم ربّك الأعلى is from the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā. Allah knows best what He intended; but the view of Qatāda is good because it refers to what immediately precedes it, and the way of a thing is that it refers to what is next to it, unless a decisive proof comes that changes that.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: [صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى is genitive] as a badal (substitute). الصحيفة is the written book.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
الَّذِي خَلَقَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الأعلى, or, if you wish, of ربك. It is permissible to qualify an adjective, because in meaning it is the thing qualified; on this basis يا يزيد الكريم ذو الجمّة ("O noble Yazīd with the long locks") is permissible. The meaning of الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى is "who created the creatures and proportioned their form, so that all of it became good in what was made".
وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ, i.e. He determined their forms, their provisions and their deeds. فَهَدى: it was said: so He made clear to them. It was also said: the meaning is "so He guided and led astray". It was also said: so He guided them to their interests.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى is] in the position of the genitive, conjoined. المرعى is what the beasts eat.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: [غُثاءً أَحْوى are] two objects. There are two views about it. One of them: "and who brought out the pasture, dark (أحوى), i.e. green verging on black, then made it stubble". The other view: "and who brought out the pasture and then made it black stubble". This is nearer to correctness; fronting and postponing [of words] only occurs when the meaning cannot be sound otherwise — especially since Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فجعله غثاء أحوى — he is saying: dry, withered and changed.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: There are two views about it. One of them: "so you will not leave [it]". The other is that it is from forgetting (النسيان). This is preferable, because the exegetes hold it. Mujāhid said: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite to himself so as not to forget. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb said: Mālik ibn Anas narrated to me concerning His saying سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى: he said: you will memorise, «except what Allah wills». The meaning in both views together is "you will not forget"; it is a statement, not a prohibition. According to the greatest of the lexicographers it is not permissible for a person to be forbidden to forget, because forgetting is not in his control.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ is in the position of the accusative as the excepted. There are several views on its meaning. On the first answer: you will not leave anything of what Allah commanded you except what Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, wills that We abrogate, so that He commands you to leave it and you leave it. It was also said: you will not forget except what Allah wills you to forget, and Allah does not will that you forget any of it.
This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who likened it to His saying خالِدِينَ فِيها ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ [Hūd: 107]. It was also said: the meaning is "you will not forget except what Allah wills of what befalls human beings". It was also said: you will not forget except what Allah wills to lift up and to lift its recitation. These are four answers. A fifth answer is that the meaning is "then He made it dark stubble, except what Allah wills". Allah knows best what He intended. إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ, i.e. what is manifest and open, وَما يَخْفى, what is concealed and hidden; i.e. so do not commit acts of disobedience to Him, for He knows what is outward and what is inward.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: That is, for the easiest state.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: There are two views about it. One of them: "so remind in every case, whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit", like سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ [al-Naḥl: 81] [where the cold is understood as well]. The other answer is that the reminder benefits in every case, so the meaning is as you say: "remind, if you are doing what you were commanded".
